newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania July inflation drops to record low 0.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: Romania July inflation drops to record low 0.7 pct.

text.p: Romania's July inflation fell to a record low 0.7 percent from June's 2.3 percent, lower than forecasts between 1.0 and 1.5 percent, the National Statistics Board (CNS) said on Friday.
It said year-on-year July inflation dropped to 159.8 percent from 177.4 percent in June. Consumer prices rose 102.6 percent from December 1996.
July's figure was the lowest since October 1990, when prices were first freed in Romania after the 1989 fall of communism.
Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea said on Thursday monthly inflation would probably be between one and two percent until the end of 1997, down from previous forecasts of two to three percent.

Officials also had revised up the 1997 year-on-year inflation to about 130 percent from a previous estimate of 90 percent. Their revisions followed higher-than-expected prices rises in February and March when the centrist coalition government liberalised fuel, energy and staples prices.
